counting_rule: 166 stroke cards from MER manuals 1–5. Variants and opening/closing holds are included; these are not 166 unique techniques.

cards.title: Posterior neck work (1)
cards.explanation: Starting from the 7th Cervical vertabrea, stretching the lateral mass of muscles, the Trapezius, the Erectus Spinae muscles, Splenius Capitis, Splenius Cervicis and the deep intrinsic muscles. Sensing the holding pattern, move deep and slowly stretching up to the base of the Occiput. Spend time there releasing the tension by holding it.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Posterior neck work (2)
cards.explanation: You can also work the right side of the neck with the left hand and the other way around. Place your hand under the neck and curl your fingers next to the spine. Then find your depth and slowly stretch out with your hand until you come to the base of the Occiput. Spend time there releasing the tension by holding it.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Posterior neck work (3)
cards.explanation: Place your finger tips at the level the 3th Thoracic Vertabrae on the side of the spine. It is a good option to hold this spot for a while to release the expression that is often locked there. Then find your depth and slowly stretch out with your right hand until you come to the base of the Occiput.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Cranial/occipital decompression
cards.explanation: Pressure is applied upwards at the base of the Occiput. Fingers are curved, with a pressure coming from the tips. The Occiput resting on your palms. Sometimes you have to wait several minutes to feel the softening and the decompression.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Trapezius: soft knuckles
cards.explanation: With your two right (soft) knuckles, from the top (working down), hook the top of the Trapezius, and with the other hand stretch the neck in the opposition. Repeat this 4 to 5 times in different spots.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Suboccipital muscle
cards.explanation: Turn the client’s head to the opposite side you are working. With the right thumb stroke below the posterior aspect of the Mastoid Process, sliding down to the Posterior Suboccipital muscle below the middle of the Occiput.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Sternocleidomastoid
cards.explanation: With the finger tips or thumbs, with the client having turned the head in the opposite direction slide slowly and deeply on the SCM from the Mastoid Process untill you reach the Clavicle. Keep your hand at a oblique angle. Very important again to work the tendinous insertion on either side.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: SCM attachments
cards.explanation: Work with your finger tips on the insertion at the Clavicle, having the client breath in this area. Very important again to work the tendinous insertion on either side.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Make contact with the client
cards.explanation: Make contact with the client with conscious touch. Breathe into your heart and out into your hands. Fully concentrate into the meditation.

cards.title: Erectors: palms
cards.explanation: Working with the palm of the hand down the Erectors. Slowly move down using your weight going down through your hand into the fascia of the back. Move slowly with their breathe having them breath deeply into your hands. Slowly move down on one side, then the other, and then let your hands dance down together.

cards.title: Erectors: fingertips
cards.explanation: With the finger tips you can be more specific, you can have more sense of what you are sensing. Move slowly down with your finger tips on the different parts of the back. Use their breath and invite unwinding. Use short strokes, and find pain points. Move down the back with one side, and then the other, or alternate, untill you get through the Lower Back into the Sacrum.

cards.title: Erectors: back of the hand
cards.explanation: With the back of the hand, you have another tool which is very powerful and sensitive (and adaptable). Learn to keep your hand ﬁrm and soft at the same time. When you use the back of your hand, find ways that you don’t tighten the lower arm and hand. Keep them resilient so they respond to the holding patterns in the back. Move down the whole back with long or short strokes, or combine them.

cards.title: Erectors: transverse strokes
cards.explanation: With both hands right on the side of the Spineous Process, have them breath deeply when you sink into the Erectors, easing your way, slide transverse into the lateral sides of the back. Moving slowly with depth and sensitivity using their breathing and asking them to move to unwind around your touch (moving pelvis, legs,...). Allow the movement and the breath to connect to the strokes.

cards.title: Erectors: forearm
cards.explanation: Work with a broad forearm, along the side of the spine, your left foot forward and your right foot back. Push from your back foot through your right elbow along the side of the spine. Keeping a soft right hand. Slowly slide along the lateral mass next to the spine, as the client breaths into your forearm.

cards.title: Superior trapezius: palm
cards.explanation: With the palm of your right hand on their left side of the Upper Trapezius, your left foot forward and the left hand back, fall with your right hand into the trapezius, move from C7 into the Scapula. Have the client breathe into your touch and unwind the body.

cards.title: Superior trapezius: back of hand
cards.explanation: Working the top part of the Trapezius down to where it attaches to the Scapula. Work on the left side with your left hand, your right foot forward (your foot should be behind your hand). The client can stretch the arm down, as it increases the stretch. Stroke down over the top of the Shoulder Girdle, being aware of softening your hand when you are over the bone.
cautions: Soften the hand over bone.

cards.title: Levator scapulae: thumbs
cards.explanation: Move your thumb to the Upper Trapezius, circle the neck with your fingers, lightly, and then work with your thumb, deep into the Levator Scapulae. Work for a while into the LS until it releases. Work deep into the Trapezius where it inserts at the Medial and Anterior border of the Scapula. Continue to slide up the Posterior Transverse Process of the Cervical Vertebrae.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Lower back: thumb and breath
cards.explanation: Use your thumbs over the Lateral Mass between the Spineous process and the Transverse Process, you can support your thumb with the fingers of the other hand. Feel the places where there is less movement of the breath. Have the client breath into your thumb and stay there for at least 30 sec. working with their breath. As they are breathing, ask them to move their spine around your thumb.

cards.title: Psoas
cards.explanation: Bring the finger tips of your left hand to the Anterior Iliac Spine. Make a line to the navel. Place the finder pads of your left hand at the level of 1/3th of the line from the Anterior Spine to the navel. With the fingers of you right hand on top of your left hand for support. Drop your weight slowly through your fingers, ask your client to raise his leg so you can feel the Psoas contract. Have the client place their foot on the table in neutral position. Stretch the Psoas up with your finger tips to the level of their Umbilicus. Ask your client to rock the Pelvis into full flection and extension, while you stretch the Psoas.
cautions: Wait until the client knows the work after a few sessions; do not overwork; allow integration.

cards.title: Gluteal attachments on posterior iliac bone
cards.explanation: Working with the backs of both hands, slowly slide towards the Greater Trocanter with the right hand and with the left around the Crest of the Ilium.

cards.title: Gluteus maximus, medius, minimus: forearm
cards.explanation: Bring your forearm across your body, and stretch down the Gluteus Maximus towards the feet right into the insertion on the Upper Femur. Then work the Gluteus Medius moving your elbow laterally on the Crest of the Ilium, stroking slowly down the Greater Trocanter. If possible go still deeper into the Gluteus Minimus. Bring the knee in flexion and move the foot which rotates the hip joint under your touch.

cards.title: Gluteal insertion
cards.explanation: Working the insertion into the Greater Trocanter of all three gluteals with your finger tips. Work slowly stay deep and sensitive.

cards.title: Thoracic inlet hold
cards.explanation: Place the right hand on the Clavicle on top of the Sternum, and the left hand between the shoulder blades and the upper thoracic. Hold for one minute.

cards.title: Respiratory diaphragm hold
cards.explanation: Place the finger tips on top of the Xiphoid process, as you rest your hand down the middle of the Diaphragmatic Segment. The left hand slides under the middle back, as the client rests the arm above the head (use pillow if needed).

cards.title: Pelvic diaphragm hold
cards.explanation: Place your left hand on top of the belly with the edge touching the Pubic bone. Place your right hand on the Sacrum underneath the left hand.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Plantar fascia: back of hand
cards.explanation: The client lies on the belly with a pillow under the lower legs. With the back of your hand below the Calcaneus in the mid line of the foot, working down slowly through the ball of the foot. Repeat the stroke on the Lateral Arch. (Postural cue: Right hand on right foot, left foot in front)

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Malleoli and Achilles sides: fingertips
cards.explanation: With the client lying on his stomach, work with the finger tips, all around the Lateral Malleoli and along the side of the Achilles tendon. Repeat the stroke on the Medial Malleolis and up the side of the Achilles tendon with the left hand.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Gastrocnemius: back of hand
cards.explanation: With the back of the loose right hand, starting from the Calcaneus, slowly stroke up the Gastrocnemius, finishing with a soft pressure at the back of the knee.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Gastrocnemius: fingertips
cards.explanation: With the finger tips of both hands, seperate the two bellies of the Gastrocnemicus working up the knee.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Gastrocnemius attachments: fingertips
cards.explanation: Work the Gastrocnemicus attachment on the condyle. Slowly work with the finger tips on the Lateral and Medial condyles.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Middle hamstring
cards.explanation: Place the right forearm to the level of the Ischial Tuberosity in the middle of the Hamstrings. Deeply stroke down to the back of the Knee. Work slowly and with sensitivity.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Medial hamstring
cards.explanation: Move to the other side of the table. Starting with the Medial Hamstring, work from the bottom of the Pelvis slowly and deeply with a ﬂat right forearm, down to the attachment on the Tibia.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Lateral hamstring
cards.explanation: With the left elbow crossing your body, standing with the left leg forward, slide down the Lateral part of the Hamstring, from the Pelvis to the Knee.
muscles: biceps femoris long and short heads

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Hamstring attachment: ischial tuberosity
cards.explanation: Working with your finger tips on the Ischial Tuberosity, ask the client to raise their lower leg up bending the knee feeling for the Hamstring Attachments. Work deeply sliding slowly medially. Work for about 1 minute.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Plantar fascia: thumbs and knuckles, three arches
cards.explanation: When the client is on the back, there is also much room to work deeply with the thumbs and knuckles on the Plantar fascia and the muscles of the foot. Starting with the knuckles and the thumbs, move down the foot through the Medial arch, to the Middle of the foot and to the Lateral arch. As you do it grab the toes of the foot and the ball of the foot and stretch down towards the leg.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Plantar fascia: medial arch with toe stretch
cards.explanation: With the knuckles or the thumb of the left hand on the Medial arch, slowly slide up to the ball of the foot while stretching the toes back with the right hand.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Achilles and ankle movement
cards.explanation: With the clients left foot sitting on your right leg, work with the fingers of the right hand on the side of the Achilles Tendon. In between the strokes hold the top of the foot and rotate the foot and ankle in different positions for maximum stretch and movement.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Dorsal surface of foot
cards.explanation: With the client lying on his/her back: while sitting behind the left foot, holding the foot with the fingers, working with both thumbs down the Extensor Digitorum Longus Tendons of the 2nd through the 5th toe to the ankle. When working this area you can follow up the strokes by lightly rotating and gently squeezing the foot.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Peroneus: back of hand
cards.explanation: Stand facing the right foot, with the back of the right hand slide slowly down the Lateral line of the lower leg. Releasing the Peroneus from the Head of the Fibula down the Lateral shaft to External Malleolus.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Peroneus: thumbs
cards.explanation: Working with the left thumb on the right leg slowly work the Peroneus down to the Middle of the ankle.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Extensor digitorum longus and tibialis anterior: back of hand
cards.explanation: Working with the back of the right hand on the right leg, work lateral to the Tibialis Anterior down to the middle of the ankle.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Extensor digitorum longus and tibialis anterior: fingertips
cards.explanation: Facing the foot of the left side, working with the right leg, place your finger tips on the inside of the Medial side of the Tibia, working slowly and deeply down to the middle of the ankle.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Medial knee: fingertips
cards.explanation: Working on the right knee with the right hand on the Medial surface of the knee, work deep and slow. Often I have people lift their knee up and down as I work, repeat that stroke 2 or 3 times. With knee pain, stay on the point of pain with appropriate pressure.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Medial edge of patella: thumb
cards.explanation: Working on the right knee with the right thumb on the Medial surface of the patella working deep and slow, often I have people lift their knee up and down as I work, repeat that stroke 2 or 3 times. With knee pain, stay on the point of pain with appropriate pressure. Work all through the inside knee with the tumb.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Lateral edge of patella: fingertips
cards.explanation: Working on the right knee with the finger tips on the Lateral surface of the Patella, work deep and slow. Often I have people lift their knee up and down as I work, repeat that stroke 2 or 3 times. With knee pain, stay on the point of pain with appropriate pressure. Work all through the Lateral knee with the finger tips.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Knee joint mobilisation
cards.explanation: With ons hand on the top of the knee and the other at the bottom compress and rotate the Knee joint. For about 30 seconds, keep compressing and rotating. If the knee has pain, work sensitively with this and compress the knee in the area where there is pain.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Quadriceps: palm
cards.explanation: Start from the Knee and slowly move up the Quadriceps with your palm.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Rectus femoris
cards.explanation: Working with the back of your hand from the Patella to the attachment of the Rectus Femoris to the Anterior Inferior Iliac Spine (AIIS).

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Vastus lateralis
cards.explanation: With the left hand working on the right leg, starting from the Lateral aspect of the Patella pushing from your back leg through your hand towards the Greater Trocanter.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the feet / legs and knees
cards.title: Gluteals: back of hand
cards.explanation: Working with the backs of both hands, slowly slide towards the Greater Trocanter with the right hand and with the left around the crest of the Ilium.

cards.title: Make contact with the client
cards.explanation: Make contact with the client with conscious touch. Breathe into your heart and out into your hands. Fully concentrate into the meditation.

cards.title: Erectors: palms
cards.explanation: Working with the palm of the hand down the Erectors. Slowly move down using your weight going down through your hand into the fascia of the back. Move slowly with their breathe having them breath deeply into your hands. Slowly move down on one side, then the other, and then let your hands dance down together.

Move down the back with one side, and then the other, or alternate, untill you get through the Lower Back into the Sacrum.

cards.explanation: Work with a broad forearm, along the side of the spine, your left foot forward and your right foot back. Push from your back foot through your right elbow along the side of the spine. Keeping a soft right hand. Slowly slide along the lateral mass next to the spine, as the client breaths into your forearm.

cards.title: Superior trapezius: palm
cards.explanation: With the palm of your right hand on their left side of the Upper Trapezius, your left foot forward and the left hand back, fall with your right hand into the trapezius, move from C7 into the Scapula. Have the client breathe into your touch and unwind the body.

cards.title: Superior trapezius: back of hand
cards.explanation: Working the top part of the Trapezius down to where it attaches to the Scapula. Work on the left side with your left hand, your right foot forward (your foot should be behind your hand). The client can stretch the arm down, as it increases the stretch. Stroke down over the top of the Shoulder Girdle, being aware of softening your hand when you are over the bone.
cautions: Soften the hand over bone.

cards.title: Posterior neck work (1)
cards.explanation: Starting from the 7th Cervical vertabrea, stretching the lateral mass of muscles, the Trapezius, the Erectus Spinae muscles, Splenius Capitis, Splenius Cervicis and the deep intrinsic muscles. Sensing the holding pattern, move deep and slowly stretching up to the base of the Occiput. Spend time there releasing the tension by holding it.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Posterior neck work (2)
cards.explanation: You can also work the right side of the neck with the left hand and the other way around. Place your hand under the neck and curl your fingers next to the spine. Then find your depth and slowly stretch out with your hand until you come to the base of the Occiput. Spend time there releasing the tension by holding it.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Lower back: forearm
cards.explanation: Facing the feet, place the ﬂat right forearm at the Lumbar Dorsal Hinge, slide deeply down the lower back until you get to the Sacrum. If your client has got lower back pain, work for at least one minute deeply on the area of the pain, asking the client to breath into the stroke.

cards.title: Superior trapezius: back of hand
cards.explanation: Working the top part of the Trapezius down to where it attaches to the Scapula. Work on the left side with your left hand, your right foot forward (your foot should be behind your hand). The client can stretch the arm down, as it increases the stretch. Stroke down over the top of the Shoulder Girdle, being aware of softening your hand when you are over the bone.
cautions: Soften the hand over bone.

cards.title: Lower back: thumb and breath
cards.explanation: Use your finger tips or thumbs over the Lateral Mass between the Spineous process and the Transverse Process. Feel the places where there is less movement of the breath. Have the client breathe into your finger tips or thumbs and stay there for at least 30 sec. working with their breath. As they are breathing, ask them to move their spine around your thumb.

cards.title: Sacrum: fingertips
cards.explanation: With the finger tips of both hands, work the Sacral Fascia slowly while asking the client to breathe into your fingers and encourage them to move around your fingers with their Pelvis.

cards.title: Gluteus medius and maximus attachments
cards.explanation: Working with the backs of both hands, slowly slide towards the greater trocanter with the right hand and with the left around the crest of the Ilium.

cards.title: Piriformis
cards.explanation: Sitting on the table next to the client facing the feet. Stretch the lower leg lateral and work with your forearm from the side of the Sacrum, stroke down deeply underneath the Gluteus, to the Greater Grocanter.

cards.title: Gemellus superior and inferior
cards.explanation: Working on the Gemellus-twins, with the back of your hands sliding from the Ischial Tuberosity to the upper border of the Greater Trochanter.

cards.title: Obturator internus and externus
cards.explanation: With the elbow or the finger tips, from the Ischial Tuberosity and the basis of the pubic, work deeply towards the Greater Trochanter.

cards.title: Quadratus femoris
cards.explanation: Sitting on the table next to the client facing the feet. Stretch the lower leg lateral and work with your elbow from the lateral edge of the Ischial Tuberosity to the Greater Trocanter.

cards.title: Sacrum and gluteal fascia: fingertips
cards.explanation: With the finger tips on top of the Sacral fascia, use oblique strokes spreading the fascia from the Medial Sacrum laterally into the Gluteus fascia.

cards.title: Middle hamstring
cards.explanation: Place the right forearm to the level of the Ischial Tuberosity in the middle of the Hamstrings. Deeply stroke down to the back of the Knee. Work slowly and with sensitivity.

cards.title: Medial hamstring
cards.explanation: Move to the other side of the table. Starting with the Medial Hamstring, work from the bottom of the Pelvis slowly and deeply with a ﬂat right forearm, down to the attachment on the Tibia.

cards.title: Lateral hamstring
cards.explanation: With the left forearm crossing your body, standing with the left leg forward, slide down the Lateral part of the Hamstring, from the Pelvis to the Knee.
muscles: biceps femoris long and short heads

cards.title: Pelvic floor
cards.explanation: With the person lying on the side, with the fingers of your hands slowly and with sensitivity feel for the bottom of the Coccyx, the inside of the sit bones and the bottom of the Pubic bone. These are the attachments of the Pelvic ﬂoor muscles. Work underneath the Coccyx releasing the muscle and then turn your finger tips up and hook the Coccyx, pulling it out softly, to help straighten the Coccyx.

cards.title: Rib attachments of rectus abdominis
cards.explanation: Bring your fingers just above the costal arch, on the 7th Rib at the level of the Xiphoid Process. With the finger pads of both hands, contact the R.A. attachments and stretch up while the client breaths deeply into your fingers.

cards.title: Rectus abdominis: pubic attachment
cards.explanation: With the finger tips of your right hand contact the Crest of the right side of the Pubic Bone. Stretch the tissue slowly and with sensitivity, having your client breath deeply into the belly. Move medially to the Pubic Symphysis. Stay with the stroke for at least thirty sec, asking your client to breath into your fingers.

cards.title: Rectus abdominis: fingertips
cards.explanation: With the finger tips of your left hand, starting from the Costal Arch and sliding down to the the Pubic Crest with your hand at a horizontal level on the muscle until you get to the Pubic Attachments.

cards.title: External oblique on iliac crest: back of hand
cards.explanation: Facing the right side of the Rectus Abdominis, with your right foot forward, place the back of your right hand on the lateral margin of the R.A. Stretch slowly down with the back of your hand over the Iliac Crest to the table.

cards.title: External and internal oblique: back of hand
cards.explanation: Standing over the left shoulder, facing down towards the feet, place the back of your right hand on the Ribs from the bottom of the Costal Arch, slowly stretch down towards the armpit, as you ask your client to breath into the Ribs.

cards.title: Internal oblique: fingertips
cards.explanation: Have your client’s legs resting on a pillow. Find the Anterior Superior Iliac Spine at the Crest of the Ilium. With the finger tips of the right hand move up towards the lower Ribs stretching the Internal Oblique.

cards.title: Diaphragm work: fingertips and thumbs
cards.explanation: Have the client’s knees lift up in a neutral position, about shoulders width. Work the Diaphragm muscle on the client’s right side, with your left hand. Bring your fingertips underneath the Rib Cage, while your right hand cradles the Rib Cage from the top bringing it down and in towards your working hand, creating space while your left hand stays deep. Work from the bottom up staying with each segment through the time of three or four breaths. Have them breath in their chest not the belly. Move 3 segments up to the solar plexus. In between, you can gently hold the back and the front of the area you have been working.

cards.title: Respiratory diaphragm hold
cards.explanation: Place the finger tips on top of the Xiphoid process, as you rest your hand down the middle of the Diaphragmatic Segment. The left hand slides under the middle back, as the client rests the arm above the head (use pillow if needed).

cards.title: Linea alba: fingertips
cards.explanation: Contact the Linea Alba between the left and the right side of the Rectus Abdominis, at the level of the Costal Arch. Slowly stretch down the Linea Alba, stretching all the way to the Pubic Bone. Work slowly and with sensitivity, with the client’s breath.

cards.title: Psoas
cards.explanation: Bring the finger tips of your left hand to the Anterior Iliac Spine. Make a line to the navel. Place the finder pads of your left hand at the level of 1/3th of the line from the Anterior Spine to the navel. With the fingers of you right hand on top of your left hand for support. Drop your weight slowly through your fingers, ask your client to raise his leg so you can feel the Psoas contract. Have the client place their foot on the table in neutral position. Stretch the Psoas up with your finger tips to the level of their Umbilicus. Ask your client to rock the Pelvis into full ﬂection and extension, while you stretch the Psoas.
cautions: Wait until the client knows the work after a few sessions; do not overwork; allow integration.

cards.title: Gluteal attachments on posterior iliac bone
cards.explanation: Working with the backs of both hands, slowly slide towards the Greater Trocanter with the right hand and with the left around the Crest of the Ilium.

cards.title: Lesser trochanter: fingertips
cards.explanation: Bring your right knee up the table, place the client’s back of the right leg on your thigh, while you finger tips move in, towards the hip joint, until you feel a round surface of the Lesser Trocanter.

cards.title: Iliopsoas stretch
cards.explanation: Have your client lie on the right side with the pillow under the head. With your left hand lift your client’s left leg. Hold under the knee, with their lower leg resting on the side of your arm. Your right hand is placed at the back of L4 L5. Stretch back the client’s left leg with your left hand and push gently forward into the spine with your right hand, bringing the body into hyperextension. Hold for thirty sec, asking the client to breath into the stretch.
cautions: Wait until the client knows the work after a few sessions; do not overwork; allow integration.

cards.title: Umbilicus
cards.explanation: Position your client with the knees up and feel for the outer edges of the Rectus. Bring your finger tips slowly underneath the Rectus until you contact the Umbilicus Fascia. Slowly bring your fingers together. When your finger tips are in contact with each other, the tissue on the inner aspect of the Umbilicus will be between your fingers. Slowly with sensitivity lift the Umbilicus towards the ceiling and towards the head. The Umbilicus is a rich source of emotional connection as well as fascial ones.

cards.title: Pelvic lift
cards.explanation: Have your client push up into an arch. Bring your left hand to the lower abdomen and the right hand to the sacrum. As they come down with their back to the table hold that position and slowly slide your right hand down stretching the lower back and sacrum.

cards.title: Posterior neck work (1)
cards.explanation: Starting from the 7th Cervical vertabrea, stretching the lateral mass of muscles, the Trapezius, the Erectus Spinae muscles, Splenius Capitis, Splenius Cervicis and the deep intrinsic muscles. Sensing the holding pattern, move deep and slowly stretching up to the base of the Occiput. Spend time there releasing the tension by holding it.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Posterior neck work (2)
cards.explanation: You can also work the right side of the neck with the left hand and the other way around. Place your hand under the neck and curl your fingers next to the spine. Then find your depth and slowly stretch out with your hand until you come to the base of the Occiput. Spend time there releasing the tension by holding it.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Posterior neck work (3)
cards.explanation: Place your finger tips at the level the 3th Thoracic Vertabrae on the side of the spine. It is a good option to hold this spot for a while to release the expression that is often locked there. Then find your depth and slowly stretch out with your right hand until you come to the base of the Occiput.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Cranial/occipital decompression
cards.explanation: Pressure is applied upwards at the base of the Occiput. Fingers are curved, with a pressure coming from the tips. The Occiput resting on your palms. Sometimes you have to wait several minutes to feel the softening and the decompression.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Adductors: back of hand
cards.explanation: Starting with the back of the right hand at the inside of the knee, slowly slide up the length of the Adductors to the attachments at the Pelvis. Work three lines up: Posterior, Medial and Anterior (back, middle and front).

cards.title: Ischial tuberosity to pubic symphysis: fingertips
cards.explanation: With the finger pads of the right hand starting from the Ischial Tuberosity, slide in and forward along the bone all the way to the Pubic Symphysis. Feeling for the tendons and fascial bands, work slowly with very sensitive finger tips. Stay with this area for a few minutes.
muscles: tendons and fascial bands along ischial-pubic region

cards.title: Hip joint stretch
cards.explanation: Slowly take the leg laterally and keep stretching down toward the table with the lower leg perpendicular to the upper leg. Hold the bottom of the foot and push the knee gently down towards the table. The right hand anchors the client’s right leg.

cards.title: Hamstring stretch
cards.explanation: Come up on the table, with your left knee supporting the client’s right knee, keeping it locked. With your left hand on the ball of the foot and right hand on the heel, move the leg up until you meet their resistance. Hold for 15 seconds.

cards.title: Side twist for lumbar spine
cards.explanation: Come up on the table with your right knee behind the client’s Pelvis, and your left foot resting gently on the right shoulder. With your right hand on the thigh and your left hand on the back of the Pelvis twist the leg and Pelvis until you meet resistance. Hold for 15 seconds.

cards.title: Posterior neck work (1)
cards.explanation: Starting from the 7th Cervical vertabrea, stretching the lateral mass of muscles, the Trapezius, the Erectus Spinae muscles, Splenius Capitis, Splenius Cervicis and the deep intrinsic muscles. Sensing the holding pattern, move deep and slowly stretching up to the base of the Occiput. Spend time there releasing the tension by holding it.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Posterior neck work (2)
cards.explanation: You can also work the right side of the neck with the left hand and the other way around. Place your hand under the neck and curl your fingers next to the spine. Then find your depth and slowly stretch out with your hand until you come to the base of the Occiput. Spend time there releasing the tension by holding it.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Posterior neck work (3)
cards.explanation: Place your finger tips at the level the 3th Thoracic Vertabrae on the side of the spine. It is a good option to hold this spot for a while to release the expression that is often locked there. Then find your depth and slowly stretch out with your right hand until you come to the base of the Occiput.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Cranial/occipital decompression
cards.explanation: Pressure is applied upwards at the base of the Occiput. Fingers are curved, with a pressure coming from the tips. The Occiput resting on your palms. Sometimes you have to wait several minutes to feel the softening and the decompression.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Trapezius: soft knuckles
cards.explanation: With your two right (soft) knuckles, from the top (working down), hook the top of the Trapezius, and with the other hand stretch the neck in the opposition. Repeat this 4 to 5 times in different spots.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Suboccipital muscle
cards.explanation: Turn the client’s head to the opposite side you are working. With the right thumb stroke below the posterior aspect of the Mastoid Process, sliding down to the Posterior Suboccipital muscle below the middle of the Occiput.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Sternocleidomastoid
cards.explanation: With the finger tips or thumbs, with the client having turned the head in the opposite direction slide slowly and deeply on the SCM from the Mastoid Process untill you reach the Clavicle. Keep your hand at a oblique angle. Very important again to work the tendinous insertion on either side.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: SCM attachments
cards.explanation: Work with your finger tips on the insertion at the Clavicle, having the client breath in this area. Very important again to work the tendinous insertion on either side.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Anterior scalene
cards.explanation: Palpate with your fingers for the Anterior Scalene and slowly add pressure. Slide over the belly of the muscle. The Anterior Scalene arises from the anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the third, fourth, ﬁfth, and sixth cervical vertebrae,
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.
Nerves run through this area toward the arm; monitor responses.

cards.title: Middle scalene
cards.explanation: Palpate with your fingers for the Medial Scalene and slowly add pressure. Slide over the belly of the muscle. The Middle scalene arises from the posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the lower six cervical vertebrae.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.
Nerves run through this area toward the arm; monitor responses.

cards.title: Posterior scalene
cards.explanation: Palpate with your fingers for the Posterior Scalene and slowly add pressure. Slide over the belly of the muscle. It arises, by two or three separate tendons, from the posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the lower two or three cervical vertebrae.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.
Nerves run through this area toward the arm; monitor responses.

cards.title: Infrahyoid: soft fingertips
cards.explanation: The Infrahyoid Muscles are located on the anterior neck superficial to the Trachea. Starting from the top of the Sternum, next to the Trachea, going very slowly with the (soft) finger tips of your left hand stroke upwards to the base of the Hyoid bone.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Pectoralis major (1): medial insertion
cards.explanation: Gently work the superficial structure of the Costal and Sternal connection. Start right on the front of the chest along the Costal Ridge and work slowly having the client breath into your fingers. Work at about 30 degrees angle, up towards the top of the Sternal Clavicular Joint.

cards.title: Pectoralis major (2)
cards.explanation: With the your right hand slowly stretch the Pectoralis Major laterally and underneath the Clavicle towards the Humerus. Stroke the Clavicle attachment at the Sternum, moving towards the Anterior Deltoid Muscle.

cards.title: Pectoralis major (3): knuckles
cards.explanation: Facing the clients head bring the loose knuckles of your right hand underneath the Clavicle at the level of the Sternum. Slide down the Pectoralis Major by leaning your body over until you get to the Deltoid. Be aware of the Coracoid Process.
cautions: Be aware of / do not run over the coracoid process.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the face and cervical area
cards.title: Frontalis
cards.explanation: Stretching the Frontalis muscle on the forehead up into the front of the Scalp, with the finger tips or the thumbs. Work the whole forehead.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the face and cervical area
cards.title: Posterior attachments of mandible
cards.explanation: With the finger tips of the left hand go deep under the middle of the chin, hooking the muscle and stretching down the Mandible towards the ear. Work very slowly with sensitivity.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the face and cervical area
cards.title: Zygomatic arch
cards.explanation: Place your finger tips beside the nose curling into the Zygomatic Arch and slide back to the level of the Temporal bone.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the face and cervical area
cards.title: Fascia at side of scalp
cards.explanation: With the finger tips of both hands, work up the side of the Scalp with circular strokes, without sliding so you do not pull the client’s hair. Start on the Temporalis and work your way down. This is very soothing for people with headaches.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.
Use circular contact without sliding, to avoid pulling hair.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the face and cervical area
cards.title: Sphenoid hold
cards.explanation: Cup your hands underneath the Occiput and both thumbs at the wing of the Sphenoid. Gently lift up feeling for movement. Hold for about 30 sec.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the face and cervical area
cards.title: Masseter: outside work
cards.explanation: With the finger tips of your hand, anchored by the thumb in a counter stretch, contact the origin at the Zygomatic Arch, sliding down to the insertion at the angle at the Mandible. Ask your client to open the mouth, stretching the Masseter, while you stretch down the belly of the muscle. Work one side at a time.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the face and cervical area
cards.title: Orbit of eye
cards.explanation: Place the thumb of your right hand on the Medial Posterior Orbit of the eye and stroke laterally and slowly. You can also stretch and hold this fascia until you feel it release.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the face and cervical area
cards.title: Upper orbit of eye
cards.explanation: Place the finger tips of your right hand on the Upper Orbit curving slightly and slide laterally with sensitivity.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the face and cervical area
cards.title: Masseter and pterygoids: inside work
cards.explanation: Put on a glove when working on the inside of the mouth. Place your index finger on the inside of the cheek. Have your client tighten the jaw so you can feel the muscle contract. Feel for the upper attachments of the Maxilla, the Sphenoid and the Zygomatic Arch. Work slowly with much sensitivity on the muscle’s attachments and belly.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.
Wear a glove; work slowly and sensitively.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the face and cervical area
cards.title: Muscles of jaw
cards.explanation: Moving from the lateral side of the Mandible, down towards the chin, work slowly with the finger tips.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.segment_chapter: Working the face and cervical area
cards.title: Scalp
cards.explanation: With the thumb placed on top of the Scalp, use your fingers to release the top of the Scalp. Use your fingers to go left and right to release all different areas of the Scalp.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Erectors: superficial to deeper
cards.explanation: Just like the work with the neck, we want to start releasing the more superficial structures like the Trapezius and the Latissimus Dorsi, moving into into the deeper muscles of the back. Have the client breathe into your touch (elbow, fingers, knuckles, fist).

cards.title: Back work: broad elbow
cards.explanation: Work with a broad elbow, along the side of the spine, your right foot forward left foot back. Push from your back foot through your left elbow along the side of the spine. Keeping a soft left hand. Slowly slide along the lateral mass next to the spine, as the client breaths into your elbow.

cards.title: Superior trapezius: back of hand
cards.explanation: Working the top part of the Trapezius down to where it attaches to the Scapula. Work on the left side with your left hand, your right foot forward (your foot should be behind your hand). The client can stretch the arm down, as it increases the stretch. Stroke down over the top of the Shoulder Girdle, being aware of softening your hand when you are over the bone.
cautions: Soften the hand over bone.

cards.title: Pectoralis major: fingertips (a and b)
cards.explanation: (a) Gently work the superficial structure of the Costal and Sternal connection. Start right on the front of the chest along the costal ridge and work slowly having the client breath into your fingers. Work at about 30 degrees angle, up towards the top of the Sternal Clavicular Joint. (b) Work right under the clavicle with the finger tips, have them breath up into their first rib. Slow deep breaths. Work from the Sternum to the Acromium Process.

cards.title: Pectoralis major: palm
cards.explanation: With the your left hand slowly stretch the Pectoralis Major, laterally and underneath the Clavicle towards the Humerus. Stroke the Clavicle attachment at the Sternum, moving towards the Anterior Deltoid Muscle.

cards.title: Pectoralis major: back of hand
cards.explanation: Facing the clients head bring the loose knuckles of your left hand underneath the Clavicle at the level of the Sternum. Slide down the Pectoralis Major by leaning your body over until you get to the Deltoid. Be aware not to run over the Coracoid Process.
cautions: Be aware of / do not run over the coracoid process.

cards.title: Pectoralis minor: coracoid attachment
cards.explanation: The Pectoralis Minor is underneath the Pectoralis Major. Feel for the Coracoid Process, below the Clavicle. At the bottom of the Coracoid Process attaches the tendon of the Pectoralis Minor. Have the client bring the elbow out, and internally rotate the Humerus, it makes it easier to palpate that insertion. Work with your finger tips, deep and sensitive, while the client breaths into the upper ribs.
cautions: Be aware of / do not run over the coracoid process.

cards.title: Pectoralis minor: ribs 3 to 5
cards.explanation: Palpate the Ribs underneath the Pectoralis Major ribs 3 through 5. Take the arm and ask the client to move the arm medially. Feel the Pectoralis Minor contract. Have them breath into your fingers. Work slowly on the ribs, it is a very sensitive area.

cards.title: Anterior deltoid
cards.explanation: Use the back of your left hand, and this time your left foot is forward, your pelvis is lined behind the hand. Roll over your hand and stretch the Anterior Deltoid, with deep pressure, down to the Deltoid insertion into the Humerus. And then continue to stroke down over the lateral side of the Biceps to the elbow.

cards.title: External oblique and serratus anterior: fingertips
cards.explanation: Have your client raised their arm above their head. With the finger tips of your hand slide up the side of the Rib Cage asking the client to breath in your finger tips. Work deep and slowly. Stroke up into the Axilla. Bridge your finger tips with your thumb, to create more strength in your hand. Have them breath into your fingers the whole time.

cards.title: Oblique layers: back of hand
cards.explanation: Work with the back of the hand between the rib cage and the Pelvis. Working the different layers between the Obliques and the Transverse Abdominis. Work slowly with deep slow breaths into your hands.

cards.title: Anterior scapula
cards.explanation: Placing the back of your hand on the Anterior Scapula, ask your client to raise their arm and fingers up over their head, slowly sliding your hand up to the Axilla. Releasing the subscapularis.

cards.title: Arm and rib cage counter-stretch
cards.explanation: As you stretch the arm up over the head and down to the table or pillow, you counter stretch by pushing the Rib Cage down with your right hand. Ask the client to extend the stretch by lifting the arm over head while extending the fingers. If the arm doesn’t rest easily on the table, put pillows to support the arm, so that the client can relax. with the hand on the rib cage slide with your finger tips and palms to stretch that myofascial line. Work with their breathing.

cards.title: Triceps: back of hand
cards.explanation: Bring the arm of your client over their head, if they need a pillow to relax their arm, put one under. With the back of your hand, fingers or thumbs, stretch from the Scapula attachement to the Olecranon process of the elbow.

cards.title: Rib cage stretch
cards.explanation: Stand above the rib cage, have the client’s knees lift up in a neutral position, about shoulders width. Work the Diaphragm muscle. With the palms and thumbs of both hands push the rib cage down and reach under the costal ridge with your fingers. Release the diaphragmatic segment by pulling the Rib Cage with both hands in a slow and sensitive way. * Everyone is different, some people will not have space under the arch so it is harder to access.
cautions: Some clients have insufficient space under the costal arch for this approach.

cards.title: Diaphragm work: fingertips and thumbs
cards.explanation: Have the client’s knees lift up in a neutral position, about shoulders width. Work the Diaphragm muscle on the client’s right side, with your left hand. Bring your fingertips underneath the Rib Cage, while your right hand cradles the Rib Cage from the top bringing it down and in towards your working hand, creating space while your left hand stays deep. Work from the bottom up staying with each segment through the time of three or four breaths. Have them breath in their chest not the belly. Move 3 segments up to the solar plexus. In between, you can gently hold the back and the front of the area you have been working.

cards.title: Respiratory diaphragm hold
cards.explanation: Place the finger tips on top of the Xiphoid process, as you rest your hand down the middle of the Diaphragmatic Segment. The left hand slides under the middle back, as the client rests the arm above the head (use pillow if needed).

cards.title: Rectus abdominis: counter-strokes
cards.explanation: Your finger tips are straight and your hands are together, elbows together. Slowly open your elbows and let your hands open up. When your hands start to turn bring your elbows and finger tips together again. With both hands anchoring the tissue allow the stretch to go through your finger tips in opposing lines. Drop your weight into your finger tips.

Then find your depth and slowly stretch out with your hand until you come to the base of the Occiput. Spend time there releasing the tension by holding it.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.explanation: Place your finger tips at the level the 3th Thoracic Vertabrae on the side of the spine. It is a good option to hold this spot for a while to release the expression that is often locked there. Then find your depth and slowly stretch out with your right hand until you come to the base of the Occiput.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.explanation: Pressure is applied upwards at the base of the Occiput. Fingers are curved, with a pressure coming from the tips. The Occiput resting on your palms. Sometimes you have to wait several minutes to feel the softening and the decompression.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.explanation: With the finger tips or thumbs, with the client having turned the head in the opposite direction slide slowly and deeply on the SCM from the Mastoid Process untill you reach the Clavicle. Keep your hand at a oblique angle. Very important again to work the tendinous insertion on either side.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: SCM attachments
cards.explanation: Work with your finger tips on the insertion at the Clavicle, having the client breath in this area. Very important again to work the tendinous insertion on either side.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.explanation: Palpate with your fingers for the Anterior Scalene and slowly add pressure. Slide over the belly of the muscle. The Anterior Scalene arises from the anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth cervical vertebrae,
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.
Nerves run through this area toward the arm; monitor responses.

cards.explanation: Palpate with your fingers for the Medial Scalene and slowly add pressure. Slide over the belly of the muscle. The Middle scalene arises from the posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the lower six cervical vertebrae.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.
Nerves run through this area toward the arm; monitor responses.

cards.explanation: Palpate with your fingers for the Posterior Scalene and slowly add pressure. Slide over the belly of the muscle. It arises, by two or three separate tendons, from the posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the lower two or three cervical vertebrae.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.
Nerves run through this area toward the arm; monitor responses.

cards.explanation: Just like the work with the neck, we want to start releasing the more superficial structures like the Trapezius and the Latissimus Dorsi, moving into into the deeper muscles of the back. Have the client breathe into your touch (elbow, fingers, knuckles, fist).

cards.title: Back work: broad elbow
cards.explanation: Work with a broad elbow, along the side of the spine, your right foot forward left foot back. Push from your back foot through your left elbow along the side of the spine. Keeping a soft left hand. Slowly slide along the lateral mass next to the spine, as the client breaths into your elbow.

cards.title: Superior trapezius: back of hand
cards.explanation: Working the top part of the Trapezius down to where it attaches to the Scapula. Work on the left side with your left hand, your right foot forward (your foot should be behind your hand). The client can stretch the arm down, as it increases the stretch. Stroke down over the top of the Shoulder Girdle, being aware of softening your hand when you are over the bone.
cautions: Soften the hand over bone.

cards.title: Superior trapezius with thumbs (includes levator scapulae)
cards.explanation: Move your thumb to the upper Trapezius, cirle the neck with your fingers, lightly and the work with your thumb, deep into the Levator Scapula, deep to the Trapezius where it inserts at the Medial and Anterior border of the Scapula. Continu to slide up to the Posterior Transverse Process of the Cervical Vertabrae.
cautions: Support the head without fixing it; allow movement.

cards.title: Lumbar area: palm
cards.explanation: Work with your left hand on the client’s right side spreading the Thoracal Lumbar Fascia laterally. Your palm has an oblique contact and stretches the tissues slowly and deeply. All the time have them breath deeply into your hands.

cards.title: Gluteal attachments on posterior iliac bone
cards.explanation: Working with the backs of both hands, slowly slide towards the Greater Trocanter with the right hand and with the left around the Crest of the Ilium.

cards.title: Gluteus maximus, medius, minimus: forearm
cards.explanation: Bring your forearm across your body, and stretch down the Gluteus Maximus towards the feet right into the insertion on the Upper Femur. Then work the Gluteus Medius moving your elbow laterally on the Crest of the Ilium, stroking slowly down the Greater Trocanter. If possible go still deeper into the Gluteus Minimus. Bring the knee in flexion and move the foot which rotates the hip joint under your touch.

cards.title: Middle hamstring
cards.explanation: Place the right forearm to the level of the Ischial Tuberosity in the middle of the Hamstrings. Deeply stroke down to the back of the Knee. Work slowly and with sensitivity.

cards.title: Medial hamstring
cards.explanation: Move to the other side of the table. Starting with the Medial Hamstring, work from the bottom of the Pelvis slowly and deeply with a flat right forearm, down to the attachment on the Tibia.

cards.title: Lateral hamstring
cards.explanation: With the left forearm crossing your body, standing with the left leg forward, slide down the Lateral part of the Hamstring, from the Pelvis to the Knee.
muscles: biceps femoris long and short heads

cards.title: Ischial tuberosity: hamstring attachment
cards.explanation: Working with your finger tips on the Ischial Tuberosity, ask your client to raise their lower leg up bending the knee feeling for the Hamstring Attachments. Work deeply sliding slowly medially.

cards.title: Posterior knee: fingertips
cards.explanation: With the finger tips, either on the outside of the knee or the inside of the back of the knee, stretch down through the back of the knee, ask them to stretch out from their hip joint down towards your finger tips and straighten their knee as you stroke up the back of their knee. Connecting with slow deep breaths the whole time.

cards.title: Tensor fascia latae
cards.explanation: With the client on their side, supported by pillows, work up the Tensor fascia latae to the crest of the ilium with your forearm. Work slowly with their breathing and movement through the leg and pelvis. This is a very important muscle so spend some time with it.

cards.title: Side-lying iliotibial tract
cards.explanation: Support the clients body with pillows or bolsters. Put a pillow under their head and come up ont the table. Facing down towards the right knee slide, one at a time, your finger tips from the attachment of the Tensor Fascia Latae down the sides of the Ilio Tibial tract, releasing the attachment of the hamstrings and the quadriceps of the IT band.

cards.title: Thoracic inlet hold
cards.explanation: Place the right hand on the Clavicle on top of the Sternum, and the left hand between the shoulder blades and the upper thoracic. Hold for one minute.

cards.title: Respiratory diaphragm hold
cards.explanation: Place the finger tips on top of the Xiphoid process, as you rest your hand down the middle of the Diaphragmatic Segment. The left hand slides under the middle back, as the client rests the arm above the head (use pillow if needed).

cards.title: Pelvic diaphragm hold
cards.explanation: Place your left hand on top of the belly with the edge touching the Pubic bone. Place your right hand on the Sacrum underneath the left hand.
